data.title: Spacex Could Complete Its $60 Billion Acquisition Of Cursor As Soon As The End Of Next Week - The Information
Nvidia Stock Rises 2.2% as SpaceX Commits to Its Chips
data.description:
Nvidia , the AI chip giant powering much of the world's data-center boom, gained about 2.2% in Friday's regular session after investors cheered SpaceX's decision to build its AI platform exclusively around Nvidia hardware. Elon Musk said SpaceX expects to secure a significant share of Nvidia's GPU supply next year, immediately putting the spotlight on what could become one of Nvidia's largest AI infrastructure customers. While neither company disclosed the value or size of the deal, the message was clear: Nvidia remains the chipmaker everyone wants when building AI at scale.

The numbers show why this matters. SpaceX poured roughly $15.83 billion into AI infrastructure last quarter while generating $2.56 billion in AI revenue and expanding installed computing capacity to around 1.4 gigawatts, with even more capacity on the way. Not every dollar of that spending will land in Nvidia's pocket because AI campuses also require networking gear, power systems, cooling equipment and construction. Still, winning exclusive GPU supplier status gives Nvidia a front-row seat as one of the industry's most aggressive AI builders continues spending.

The GF Score chart only strengthens the bull case. Nvidia posts an outstanding GF Score of 95 out of 100, backed by elite profitability, explosive growth and rock-solid financial strength, all signs of a business still firing on nearly every cylinder. The only soft spot is GF Value, which suggests investors are already paying a hefty premium for that quality. That means execution matters more than ever. If SpaceX's AI expansion turns into a steady stream of GPU orders instead of a one-off deployment, Nvidia could reinforce its grip on the AI infrastructure race and give investors another reason to stay bullish despite the stock's premium valuation.

data.title: Oil Futures Settle Higher, But Down on the Week — Market Talk
Atlassian Stock Soars 32.8% as AI Users Cross One Million
data.description:
Atlassian , the workplace software company behind Jira and Confluence, delivered a blockbuster fiscal fourth quarter that sent its shares soaring about 32.8% during Friday's regular session. Revenue jumped 28% year over year to $1.77 billion, powered by 31% cloud growth as customers continued shifting workloads to its platform. AI is also becoming a meaningful growth engine, with more than 1 million monthly active users now using Atlassian's AI features after adoption more than doubled during the quarter.

The company's bottom line improved just as dramatically. GAAP net income reached $139 million, compared with a $24 million loss a year ago, while adjusted operating income surged to $636 million from $336 million, lifting the adjusted operating margin to 36% from 24%. Free cash flow totaled $475 million, equal to 27% of revenue. Full-year revenue climbed 26% to $6.57 billion, and Atlassian swung from a $130 million GAAP operating loss to a $10 million operating profit. Adding to the bullish narrative, Chief Executive Mike Cannon-Brookes plans to buy up to $250 million of Atlassian stock, putting more of his own capital behind the company's long-term strategy.

The chart makes the valuation story hard to ignore. TEAM is trading around $146 while the GF Value estimate sits near $284, implying the shares are roughly 49% below their estimated fair value. That discount alone is not a reason to buy, but it becomes much more compelling when paired with accelerating cloud growth, rapidly expanding margins and rising AI adoption. If Atlassian can keep turning AI engagement into higher customer spending instead of just more usage, today's valuation could look far more attractive in hindsight.

data.title: BANCFIRST AWARDED $400,000 TO SUPPORT AFFORDABLE HOUSING EFFORTS FOR NATIVE AMERICANS IN OKEMAH
data.description:
OKLAHOMA CITY, Aug. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Muscogee Creek Nation was one of 16 organizations selected in 2025 to receive grant funds to assist with affordable housing efforts through BancFirst, an FHLBank Topeka member. The funds are part of FHLBank Topeka's Native American Housing Initiatives (NAHI) Grants Program.

"In our capacity as a member of FHLBank Topeka, BancFirst is honored to partner with the Muscogee Nation in sponsoring their grant application for the betterment of Okemah and the Okfuskee County," said Brandon Burnett, President of BancFirst Okemah.

The grant will be used to support a planned 60-unit rental project for low-income tenants at or below 60% of the area median income.

"Due to its isolation, years of disinvestment and historical traumas faced by Tribal communities, the Muscogee Creek Nation Reservation faces an economic and housing crisis. Our Department of Housing has a waiting list of more than 500 families for our rental and lease with option to purchase programs," said Ronnie Rogers, Secretary of Housing, Muscogee Creek Nation. "These funds will make a difference in making a dent in that waiting list."

Through the 2025 program, FHLBank Topeka initially planned to award $3.6 million in grant funding to Native American tribes and tribally designated housing entities but increased the commitment following a strong response.

"We are honored to deepen our support for Native American communities in our district with $5 million in grants," said Jeff Kuzbel, FHLBank Topeka President and CEO. "The strength and vision reflected in the proposals we received from tribal nations made it clear that expanding our commitment was the right choice. Insights from our members and Native American partners following two years of our NAHI Program affirmed this flexible program is a powerful model with meaningful impact."

Visit fhlbtopeka.com/nahi to see the full list of selected projects in 2025. Applications closed in July for the 2026 NAHI grants and will be announced this fall.

About BancFirstBancFirst serves customers from 109 service locations in 64 communities across the state. More Oklahoma households bank with BancFirst than any other bank. BancFirst is the highest ranked Oklahoma bank on the 2025 Forbes list of America's Best Banks. Bank Director Magazine consistently recognizes BancFirst as a one of the safest and strongest banks in the nation. BancFirst Corporation is a publicly held company, listed on the NASDAQ National Market System under the symbol BANF. Find more information at www.bancfirst.bank.

SOURCE BancFirst

United States Commodity Index Funds Trust Q2 2026: Net income (USCI $(11.33M), CPER $65.29M), EPS (USCI $(2.90)) — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
United States Commodity Index Funds Trust reported results for the quarter ended Q2 2026 showing mixed performance across its funds: USCI recorded a loss while CPER delivered strong net income, with notable asset growth and elevated trading activity versus the year-ago quarter.

Financial Highlights

  • USCI net income (loss) was $(11.33M) for Q2 2026, compared with $3.585M in Q2 2025.
  • CPER net income was $65.29M for Q2 2026, compared with $(1.64M) in Q2 2025.
  • USCI diluted earnings per share was $(2.90) for Q2 2026, compared with $1.26 in Q2 2025.

Business Highlights

  • Fund performance: Over the most recent six months USCI and CPER posted strong NAV gains, approximately 19.29% for USCI and 8.35% for CPER, tracking their respective indexes after fees.
  • Assets & scale: The funds experienced significant AUM growth versus the prior year, with higher average daily net assets and increases in outstanding shares (approximately 3.65M additional USCI shares and 19.2M additional CPER shares year over year).
  • Trading activity & liquidity: Futures positions and brokerage activity were elevated — USCI held about 5,868 contracts across exchanges while CPER held about 4,576 contracts on COMEX, contributing to higher commission levels.
  • Revenue drivers: Higher interest income from larger cash and Treasury balances helped offset lower yields; management fees rose with asset growth, supporting operating revenue gains.
  • Operational controls & risks: The funds continued to follow index rebalancing rules and monitored regulatory margin and position limits, relying on FCMs and custodians for settlement and collateral management.

data.title: United States Brent Oil Fund, LP 2Q 2026: Net income $(208.6)M, EPS $(13.07) — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
United States Brent Oil Fund, LP reported net income of $(208.6)M for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and diluted earnings per weighted average limited partner share of $(13.07), compared with net income of $(6.19)M and EPS of $(2.02) in the year-ago quarter.

Financial Highlights

  • Net income was $(208.6)M for the three months ended June 30, 2026, versus $(6.19)M in the year-ago quarter (3Q 2025).
  • Net income for the six months ended June 30, 2026, was $(42.26)M, versus $(1.30)M in the prior-year six-month period.
  • Diluted earnings per weighted average limited partner share were $(13.07) for the quarter, compared with $(2.02) in the year-ago quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Trading exposure and strategy: The fund continued to allocate substantially all assets to Brent crude futures (7,452 ICE contracts) to track benchmark daily NAV changes.
  • NAV and price performance: Net asset value rose about 42.84% over six months to $40.41, outperforming the benchmark's hypothetical 41.10% by 1.74%.
  • Income and expense dynamics: Interest income from Treasuries and cash increased materially year over year, partially offset by management fees and higher commissions.
  • Operational controls and compliance: The fund maintained margin and collateral liquidity and complied with exchange accountability/position limits and CFTC swap/margin rules.
  • Market and risk drivers: Performance was influenced by market structure (backwardation), geopolitical supply shocks (including Iran/Strait of Hormuz developments), and oil price volatility.

data.title: United States 12 Month Natural Gas Fund, LP Q2 2026: Net income $(1.11M), EPS $(0.48) — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
United States 12 Month Natural Gas Fund, LP reported a Q2 2026 net loss of $(1.11M) and diluted loss per limited partner share of $(0.48) for the three months ended June 30, 2026, an improvement versus the year-ago quarter's net loss and $(1.53) per share; results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 showed a net loss of $(1.77M) versus net income of $1.8M in the prior-year period.

Financial Highlights

  • Net income was $(1,105,281) for Q2 2026, versus $(2,383,394) in Q2 2025 (improved YoY).
  • Net income for six months ended June 30, 2026 was $(1,765,430), versus $1,801,480 for the six months ended June 30, 2025 (YoY decline).
  • Diluted earnings per limited partner share were $(0.48) for Q2 2026, versus $(1.53) in Q2 2025.

Business Highlights

  • Benchmark tracking: The fund maintained close tracking of its 12-month natural gas futures benchmark, meeting its 30-day tracking goal (within ±10%) as of June 30, 2026.
  • Portfolio composition: Primary investments remained in NYMEX natural gas futures (510 NG contracts); no ICE or other natural gas-related investments were held during the period.
  • Income and expenses: Lower short-term yields reduced interest income and increased the net expense ratio; fees rose due to higher reporting and professional costs.
  • Liquidity and operations: The fund continued using Creation/Redemption Baskets (50,000 shares) and cash/Treasuries for margin and did not use leverage or borrowings to meet obligations.
  • Regulatory and risk posture: Management monitored exchange accountability and position limits, margin rules for swaps, and potential market disruptions from geopolitical events, weather, or pandemics.
